questions.question: Who built the Vijay Stambh in Chittorgarh?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rana Kumbha**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Vijay Stambh, also known as the Victory Tower, is located in Chittorgarh, Rajasthan, India.
 
• It was constructed by Rana Kumbha, a ruler of Mewar, in the 15th century.
 
• The tower was built to commemorate Rana Kumbha's victory over Mahmud Khilji of Malwa in 1440 AD.
 
• The Vijay Stambh is an excellent example of Rajput architecture and features intricate carvings and sculptures.
 
• The tower stands at a height of about 37 meters and has nine stories, each with balconies and windows.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Chittorgarh Fort**

 
 
• The Chittorgarh Fort, where the Vijay Stambh is located, is one of the largest forts in India.
 
• The fort has a rich history and has witnessed several battles and sieges over the centuries.
 
 
 
• **Rana Kumbha**
 
 
• Rana Kumbha was a significant ruler of Mewar and is known for his contributions to architecture and culture.
 
• He was responsible for the construction of several other notable structures, including the Kumbhalgarh Fort.
 
 
 
• **Rajput Architecture**
 
 
• Rajput architecture is characterized by its intricate carvings, large forts, and palaces.
 
• It reflects the valor, culture, and artistic achievements of the Rajput rulers.

questions.question: Which of the following Sultans of Delhi adopted the policy of Blood and Iron?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ghiyasuddin Balban**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Ghiyasuddin Balban was one of the most powerful Sultans of the Delhi Sultanate, ruling from 1266 to 1287.
 
• He is known for adopting the policy of Blood and Iron to strengthen his rule and maintain law and order.
 
• This policy involved ruthless suppression of rebellions and strict enforcement of law and discipline.
 
• Balban also reorganized the army and implemented a system of espionage to keep a check on the nobles.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Blood and Iron Policy**

 
 
• This term refers to a policy of using military force and harsh measures to maintain control and authority.
 
• Balban's implementation of this policy helped him in consolidating the fragmented empire and curbing the power of the Turkish nobles.
 
 
 
• **Espionage System**
 
 
• Balban established an extensive network of spies to gather intelligence and monitor the activities of the nobles and other officials.
 
• This system helped him prevent conspiracies and rebellions against his rule.
 
 
 
• **Reorganization of the Army**
 
 
• To ensure loyalty and efficiency, Balban restructured the army, making it a more disciplined and formidable force.
 
• He introduced a system of branding horses and maintaining a register of soldiers to prevent corruption and fraud.
 
 
 
• **Suppression of Rebellions**
 
 
• Balban's reign was marked by the suppression of various rebellions and uprisings, particularly in the regions of Bengal and Mewat.
 
• He dealt with rebels with an iron hand, often executing them to set an example for others.

questions.question: The Tamil word to describe heads of three ruling families of Cholas, Cheras and Pandyas is.
questions.solution:
The Tamil word to describe heads of three ruling families of Cholas, Cheras and Pandyas is __**Muvendar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Sangam poems** mention about the '**Muvendar**__'. 
 
• This is a **Tamil word** **meaning three chiefs, used for the heads of three ruling families, the Cholas, Cheras, and Pandyas** who became powerful in south India around 2300 years ago.
 
• Each of the three chiefs had **two centres of power: one inland, and one on the coast.**
 
• Of these six cities, two were very important: **Puhar or Kaveripattinam**, the **port of the Cholas**, and **Madurai**, the **capital of the Pandyas**.
 
• The chiefs did not collect regular taxes.
 
• Instead, they demanded and received gifts from the people.
 
• They also went on military expeditions, and collected tribute from neighbouring areas.
 
• They kept some of the wealth and distributed the rest amongst their supporters, including members of their family, soldiers, and poets.
 
• 
 
Many poets whose compositions are found in the **Sangam** collection composed poems in praise of chiefs who often rewarded them with precious stones, gold, horses, elephants, chariots, and fine cloth.

 

**Hence we can conclude that __Muvendar__ is the Tamil word used to describe heads of three ruling families of Cholas, Cheras and Pandyas.**

questions.question: Classical Indian music has its origin in which of the following?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Samaveda**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **"Sama Veda"** is an ancient Hindu scripture and one of the** four main Vedas of Hinduism.**
 
• It is a collection of melodies and chants, and is also called the** "Book of Song," "Veda of Chants" or even "Yoga of Song."**
 
• It is basically the words of the** "Rig Veda" put to music.**
 
• **Gandharvaveda **deals with various aspects of aesthetics including art forms like music, dance, poetry, sculpture, erotica etc. It is associated with Samaveda.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

**Rigveda:**

 
• The **Rig Veda** is the **earliest of the four Vedas **and one of the most important texts of the Hindu tradition. 
 
• It is a large collection of hymns in praise of the gods, which are chanted in various rituals.
 
• **Ayurveda is a Upveda of Rigveda. **

**Atharvaveda:**

 
• The Atharvaveda is commonly referred to as the** "Veda of magical formulae".**
 
• This Veda enumerates all of life's routines in great detail. 
 
• It comprises three fundamental Upanishads – Mundaka Upanishad, Mandukya Upanishad, and Prashna Upanishad – and is known as a Veda of magical formulae.

**Yajur Veda: **

 
• The **Yajur Veda (“Worship Knowledge” or “Ritual Knowledge”) **consists of recitations, ritual worship formulas, mantras, and chants directly involved in worship services.
 
• **Yajurveda was written by Veda Vyasa.**

• Gopala was the founder of the Pala Dynasty.

questions.question: Where did Chandragupta Maurya spend his last days?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Shravanabelagola**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Shravanabelagola in **Karnataka **is one of the **most-visited Jain pilgrimage spots** in South India.
 
• It is home to the **18 m high statue of Lord Gometeshwara**, one of the world's **tallest free-standing monolithic statues**.
 
 
• Constructed in **981 AD by Chamundaraya**, a Ganga warrior, it is** carved out of a single block of granite **and looms on the **top of Vindhyagiri Hill**.
 
 
 
• In **298 BCE**, **Chandragupta Maurya renounced his rule**, handing over power to his son Bindusara and traveled south to a cave at Shravanabelogola.
 
 
• There, he **meditated without eating or drinking** for **five weeks until he died of starvation** in a practice known as **sallekhana or santhara**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Pawapuri **in **Bihar **is the place of **Mahavira's nirvana** and a** pilgrimage site for Jains**.

 
 
• It is also called **Apapapuri**, meaning **'the Sinless town'**.
 
• The **Jal Mandir** meaning Water Temple, is a highly revered temple **dedicated to Lord Mahavira**, and **marks the place of his cremation**.
 
 
 
• The land of **Kashi**, also known as Varanasi or Banaras, in **Uttar Pradesh**, has been the** ultimate pilgrimage spot for Hindus** for ages.
 
 
• Hindus believe that **one who is graced to die on the land of Varanasi would attain salvation** and freedom from the cycle of birth and re-birth.
 
• The **Kashi Vishwanath Temple** is a famous Hindu temple dedicated to Lord Shiva.
 
 
 
• **Palitana **in **Gujarat **is the **world's only mountain** that has **more than 900 temples**.
 
 
• The Palitana temples and whole mountain are considered the **most sacred pilgrimage place (tirtha) by the Jain community** and is the **world's largest Temple Complex**.
